To cook (food, especially fast food), particularly by lowering into hot oil to deep-fry, or by grilling.

examples.text: Drop a basket of fries.

glosses: To reduce; to make smaller.

examples.text: Here is a simple example: suppose you are in the process of writing a 15-page proposal and at a certain point you decide that, in order to fit all your material, you want to drop the font size from 12 to 11.

glosses: Of an animal (usually a sheep): to give birth to (young); of a bird: to lay (an egg).

examples.text: to drop a lamb

glosses: To mention (something) casually or incidentally, usually in conversation.

examples.text: The lecturer would drop hints whenever the students struggled.
name drop
By 1996, ‘jungle’ and ‘drum and bass’ were the words to drop.

glosses: To let (a letter, etc.) fall into a postbox; hence, to send (a letter, email, or other message) in an offhand manner.

examples.text: As she had a free moment, she dropped her a text.
Drop me a note when you get to the city.

glosses: To make (someone or something) fall to the ground from a blow, gunshot, etc.; to bring down, to shoot down; to kill.

examples.text: Make any sudden movements and I will drop you!
That gang rules the streets, dropping opponents with guns, bombs and other weapons.

1846, ed. by G. W. Nickisson, “Elephant-Shooting in Ceylon”, in Fraser's Magazine, vol. XXXIII, no. CXCVII
page 562: ...if the first shot does not drop him, and he rushes on, the second will be a very hurried and most likely ineffectual one...
page 568 ...with a single shot he dropped him like a master of the art.
As with all other animals, a shot behind the shoulder is the most likely to drop the beast on the spot […]
He dropped the beast with a bullet in its heart.
The piano player's out, the music stopped / His boy had beef, and he got dropped...
With a quick clench of the fist on Joey's throat, Bodie dropped him. The man crumpled to the ground […]

glosses: To set down (someone or something) from a vehicle; to stop and deliver or deposit (someone or something); to drop off.

examples.text: Could you drop me at the airport on your way to work tomorrow?
I’ll be dropping the parcel at your place later.

glosses: To lower (a sound, a voice, etc.) in pitch or volume.
To lower (a sound, a voice, etc.) in pitch or volume.
To tune (a guitar string, etc.) to a lower note.
To cease concerning oneself over (someone or something); to have nothing more to do with (a discussion, subject, etc.).

examples.text: I’m tired of this subject. Will you just drop it?
They suddenly dropt the pursuit.
The connection had been dropped many years.
that astonishing ease with which fine ladies drop you and pick you up again

glosses: To dispose or get rid of (something); to lose, to remove.

examples.text: I dropped ten pounds and an obnoxious fiancée.

glosses: To cease to include (something), as if on a list; to dismiss, to eject, to expel.

examples.text: I’ve been dropped from the football team.

If Carly Telford’s replacement of Karen Bardsley, because of a hamstring injury, was enforced, the switch to 4-4-1-1 was not. This new-look configuration saw Rachel Daly deployed in front of Lucy Bronze down the right, Toni Duggan and Fran Kirby dropped, Beth Mead introduced on the left and Nikita Parris moved up front.

glosses: To cancel or cease to participate in (a scheduled course, event, or project).

examples.text: I had to drop calculus because it was taking up too much of my time.

The specialists she had taken her daughter to see attributed her collection of symptoms to the lingering effect of the many concussions she suffered playing sports. She had at least one concussion every year since she was in the fourth grade. Because of her frequent head injuries, her parents made her drop all her sports.

glosses: To lose, spend, or otherwise part with (money).

examples.text: My friends went to the football game, but I skipped, as I had just dropped a lot of money on a new bike wheel.
The question was: Who put the most in the collection box? The wealthy guy, who dropped a “C” note, or the tattered old dame who parted with her last tarnished penny.
I forked over the $19.25. I was in no position to be dropping twenties like gumdrops but I deserved something good from this crappy morning.

glosses: To pass or use (counterfeit cheques, money, etc.).
To impart (something).

examples.text: I drop knowledge wherever I go.

glosses: Especially in drop acid: to swallow (a drug, particularly LSD).
To release (a programme, software, a music album or song, etc.) to the public.

examples.text: They dropped the album Hip-Hop Xmas in time for the holidays.
That hacker has been threatening to drop my docs [i.e. publish my personal information].

glosses: To fail to write, or (especially) to pronounce (a syllable, letter, etc.).

examples.text: Cockneys drop their aitches.

glosses: To play (a portion of music) in the manner of a disc jockey.

examples.text: I love it when he drops his funky beats.
That guy can drop the bass like a monster.

glosses: To perform (rap music).

examples.text: Yo, I drop rhymes like nobody’s business.

glosses: To (unexpectedly) lose (a competition, game, etc.).
Of a fielder: to fail to dismiss (a batsman) by accidentally dropping a batted ball that had initially been caught.

examples.text: Warne dropped Tendulkar on 99. Tendulkar went on to get a century next ball.

glosses: To score (a goal) by means of a drop kick.
To cover (something) with or as if with drops, especially of a different colour; to bedrop, to variegate.

examples.text: their waved coats dropped with gold

glosses: To enter a more basic interface.

examples.text: Next, you drop to a shell.

glosses: To present (the user) with a more basic interface.

examples.text: The next step drops the user to a recovery shell.

glosses: To make someone, or be made to do push-ups or some other form of exercise on the ground as punishment.

examples.text: Drop and give me 20, now!

glosses: Downward movement, fall.
A sloping downward, e.g. of a hill or road.

examples.text: After taking a right from that turn a decline will come into view.

glosses: A deterioration of condition; a weakening or worsening.

examples.text: He has experienced a sudden decline in his health.
Educational standards are on the decline.
The country's global reputation is in decline.

In an era when political leaders promise deliverance from decline through America’s purported preeminence in scientific research, the news that science is in deep trouble in the United States has been as unwelcome as a diagnosis of leukemia following the loss of health insurance.

glosses: A reduction or diminution of activity, prevalence or quantity.

examples.text: Population decline is a major concern.
Town-centre retailers have seen a decline in footfall.

It is also pertinent to note that the current obvious decline in work on holarctic hepatics most surely reflects a current obsession with cataloging and with nomenclature of the organisms—as divorced from their study as living entities.
"It knows it has to plan for managed decline, but it can't even plan for managed decline if it doesn't know how much decline to manage."

glosses: The act of declining or refusing something.

examples.text: The issuing bank only checks the consumer's credit card number for authorization. […] Soft declines are those declines in which the bank requires further verification.

glosses: To move downwards, to fall, to drop.

examples.text: The dollar has declined rapidly since 2001.

glosses: To become weaker or worse.

examples.text: My health declined in winter.
After her sother died, Connie began to decline noticeably.

glosses: To bend downward; to bring down; to depress; to cause to bend, or fall.

examples.text: in melancholy site, with head declined
And now faire Phoebus gan decline in hast / His weary wagon to the Westerne vale.

glosses: To cause to decrease or diminish.

examples.text: You have declin'd his means.
He knoweth his error, but will not seek to decline it.

glosses: To turn or bend aside; to deviate; to stray; to withdraw.

examples.text: a line that declines from straightness
conduct that declines from sound morals

glosses: To choose not to do something; refuse, forbear, refrain.

examples.text: Could I decline this dreadful hour?

glosses: To inflect for case, number, gender, and the like.

glosses: To run through from first to last; to recite in order as though declining a noun.

examples.text: The team chose to decline the fifteen-yard penalty because their receiver had caught the ball for a thirty-yard gain.

One research team has recorded Baishui’s decrease at about 27 meters per year over the last 10 years.

glosses: Action de baisser de niveau.

examples.text: La baisse des eaux.
La baisse du baromètre semble annoncer le mauvais temps.

glosses: Diminution de prix, de valeur.

examples.text: C’est ainsi que la quasi-totalité des prix des grands produits industriels connaissent au XIXᵉ siècle un trend orienté à la baisse. Dans la sidérurgie française par exemple, les « fers et aciers ouvrés » passent de l’indice 100 en 1850 à l’indice 72 en 1911.

glosses: Diminution de valeur des monnaies, des fonds publics et des valeurs industrielles.

examples.text: La baisse du change.
Cette nouvelle a causé une grande baisse à la Bourse.
La baisse des actions.
Ces valeurs sont en baisse.

glosses: Première personne du singulier de l’indicatif présent de baisser.

examples.text: Je baisse le pare-brise pour que l’air me désétourdisse, et si je ne m’évanouis pas, c’est parce que je pense que si un agent voulait me dresser une contravention pour excès de vitesse, je pourrais lui en exhiber la raison.

glosses: Troisième personne du singulier de l’indicatif présent de baisser.

examples.text: Mais ils faut comprendre les littérateurs… ce sont des gens comme les autres… veulent tous s’exhiber, se raconter, se faire aimer, se peloter, se cuisser… en coulisses… ailleurs… salons… partout… télé… écran… petit… grand… tout tourne finalement sur le m’as-tu-vu et on baisse la culotte ensuite… avec chèque en poche bien entendu…

glosses: Première personne du singulier du subjonctif présent de baisser.

examples.text: En l’apercevant j’ai eu un mouvement de recul.
Arrive le dernier réchauffement, coïncidant avec le recul, la fonte des glaciers. Il a peu à peu conduit à un climat plus chaud et plus sec que le climat actuel : le climat xérothermique.

Raison pour quoi, comme avait si bien observé déjà mon Miroul, je n’y allais que d’une fesse, un pied déjà sur le recul, contrefeignant de ne pas apercevoir que Doña Clara dépassait avec moi — le voulant, le noulant — le seuil de l’amitié, ce que son bel œil d’un bleu profond, bordé de cils noirs, m’avait dit plus d’une fois.

glosses: Action des troupes qui se retirent d’une zone de combat.

examples.text: Sur le Continent, les fronts cèdent. Hollande, Belgique, France, le recul des troupes est général. À la débâcle fait suite l’exode massif des populations qui déferlent vers le sud.

glosses: Mouvement vers l’arrière du canon d’une arme à feu quand on tire.

examples.text: Les deux balistes tremblèrent sous le violent recul provoqué par le départ des dondaines. Les assaillis suivirent des yeux les deux mortelles flèches qui pénétrèrent dans la troupe comme des lames de fer dans de la viande molle.

glosses: Retour en arrière, régression.

examples.text: Un recul de la civilisation.

glosses: Distance suffisante dans l’espace permettant d’appréhender visuellement un objet dans son ensemble ou l’effet d’une combinaison d’éléments.

examples.text: Je n’ai pas assez de recul pour bien juger de ce tableau.

glosses: Éloignement dans le temps, permettant notamment de gagner en détachement et en perspective.

examples.text: Quand elle comprend l’importance de rester fidèle à ses aspirations, elle mesure, avec le recul, toutes les conséquences de son attitude de dévalorisation tant sentimentalement que professionnellement.
Avec le recul, c’était marrant. Je ne regrette pas d’y être allée.
Est-ce que cela aurait dû être une priorité durant l’été ? Avec du recul, vous avez sûrement raison, mais on fait ce qu’on nous dit de faire. »

glosses: Action de repousser à plus tard un événement ou la manifestation d’une chose.

examples.text: Les deux mesures ayant le plus d’impact sur l’âge de départ à la retraite sont le recul de l’âge d’ouverture des droits (AOD) et l’allongement de la durée minimale exigée pour bénéficier du taux plein et qui permet d’échapper à une minoration de pension pour trimestre manquant.

glosses: Désavantage donné à certains chevaux participants à une course de trot à conditions, que l’on fait partir en retrait des autres.
